measurement.source_commit: ccbf8100 (develop, #936 merged) + the #937 event-driven VBUS park
measurement.capacity_profile: LM20 (nRF54LM20-DK, 512 KiB SRAM; 500 KiB M33 carve; default = all-features/ble + the unconditional USB device plane; SDC size measured on glass 2026-07-24)

default.features: default (= all-features: map + router + BLE + USB device plane, LS021/FLPR, real sensors)
default._resident_note: 421,192 → 421,200 B (+8) in #937, and the whole +8 is named: `VBUS_WAKER`, the `AtomicWaker` the VREGUSB handler wakes, so `usb_named` moves 2,644 → 2,652 by exactly the same 8. Flash 1,192,944 → 1,192,864 (-80): the 500 ms timer loop cost more code than the `poll_fn` + `select` that replaced it. Poll frame unchanged at 9,728. Both figures re-measured here on the pinned host against develop at ccbf8100 rather than carried over — note develop itself measures 1,192,944 flash on this host, 8 B above the 1,192,936 recorded under #936, so the delta is the trustworthy number, not the absolute.

ble.features: --no-default-features --features ble (map + BLE + USB device plane, constrained nrf-mem capacities)
ble._resident_note: Same +8 B as `default`, from the same #937 `VBUS_WAKER` — both profiles link an identical resident set, as they have through every USB change. Flash 1,192,928 → 1,192,856 (-72, against -80 for `default`). The two profiles are *not* byte-identical in flash on this host, contrary to the #936 note above: develop measures 1,192,944 (default) vs 1,192,928 (ble) here, a spread that already existed before this change.

floating_stable_observation._comment: Hand-recorded snapshot of what CI's floating-stable toolchain links; nothing regenerates it, so it is only as current as source_commit. Both board profiles link an identical resident set, so this one observation covers them both. KNOWN STALE as of #937 (and already stale for #936 before it): it predates both the VBUS gate and the event-driven park, so expect resident 421,200 (+72) and a flash figure this observation cannot usefully predict on the next re-measure; the point it makes — floating stable links the same resident set and poll frame as the pinned toolchain — is what still holds.
